raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Accept the nested Chat Completions `tool_choice.allowed_tools` shape in the Rust frontend and restrict the renderer to the allowed function tools. Implements the roadmap item in #44280.

## Claims

- Accept `auto` and `required` modes with strict `allowed_tools` and `function` discriminators.
- Validate allowed names against top-level `tools`, then filter top-level and developer-message declarations in declaration order.
- Treat an empty `auto` list as no tools; reject an empty `required` list and undeclared functions with HTTP 400.

## Validation

Rebased onto `7f56f453e` and validated on macOS arm64 with Rust 1.95:

```bash
cd rust
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --locked -p vllm-server --lib
cargo clippy --locked -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets
cd ..
uvx pre-commit run --files \
  docs/features/tool_calling.md \
  rust/src/server/src/routes/openai/chat_completions/convert.rs \
  rust/src/server/src/routes/openai/chat_completions/types.rs \
  rust/src/server/src/routes/openai/utils/types.rs \
  rust/src/server/src/routes/tests.rs
git diff --check
```

Results: **527 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored**. Formatting, Clippy, workspace compilation, diff checks, and the complete pre-commit run passed. `cargo-nextest` was unavailable, so the library suite used `cargo test`.

For the failure check, I added the nested-shape round-trip regression to an isolated checkout of upstream `7f56f453e` and ran:

```bash
cargo test --locked -p vllm-server --lib allowed_tools_wire_shape_round_trips
```

Before the fix: `0 passed; 1 failed`, with `data did not match any variant of untagged enum ToolChoice`. The same behavior is covered by the passing library suite after the fix. HTTP tests exercise successful subset selection, required mode, empty-auto mode, malformed requests, and semantic validation against the existing scripted engine. Conversion tests inspect the exact tool list and developer declarations passed toward rendering.

The Rust Cargo Buildkite steps select the workspace tests and declare `rust/` as a source dependency. Hosted CI still requires repository authorization; the local results above do not claim a hosted CI run. No live-model evaluation was run, and no model-quality or performance claim is made.

Local environment settings selected the installed Command Line Tools and matched the Go binary to its own standard library. The earlier actionlint environment failure did not recur; the complete pre-commit run succeeded.

## Details

The current request type expects `mode` and `tools` as flat fields, while Chat Completions clients nest them under `allowed_tools`. Consequently, the nested request fails deserialization; the old flat representation also fails conversion as unsupported.

For a Rust frontend serving `served-model`, reproduce with:

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "served-model",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What time is it?"}],
    "tools": [
      {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_time", "parameters": {"type": "object"}}},
      {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"type": "object"}}}
    ],
    "tool_choice": {
      "type": "allowed_tools",
      "allowed_tools": {
        "mode": "auto",
        "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_time"}}]
      }
    }
  }'
```

Before: JSON deserialization rejects the request. After: request preparation accepts it and exposes only `get_time` as callable. The nested payload is exercised by the in-process HTTP tests; the curl command was not run against a live checkpoint.

Filtering happens before `ResolvedToolContext` and rendering. Existing duplicate-name and tool-choice resolution remain in place, and renderer, parser, and engine interfaces are unchanged. All declared tool types are validated before filtering. A developer-local tool cannot authorize an otherwise undeclared allowed name. The obsolete flat shape remains unsupported. The supported shape and edge cases are documented in `docs/features/tool_calling.md`.

The rebase preserves upstream's nullable-boolean and selected-logprob tests, adds the new `defer_loading: None` fixture fields, and updates our HTTP assertions to upstream's current error types and numeric status codes.

Duplicate checks were refreshed for `allowed_tools Rust` and `44280 in:body`. #60585 targets the Responses API, and #58783 adds the Rust Responses endpoint; neither implements this Chat Completions request path. The original scope was discussed in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44280#issuecomment-5229310963.

AI assistance was used for implementation, review, and rebasing. The submitting human reviewed and accepted the original change; the rebase-specific changes are described above for review.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill.
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Keeps filtering at the server request boundary and reuses existing tool-choice resolution.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Includes a failing upstream regression, 527 passing server tests, HTTP coverage, and documented CI and model-evaluation limits.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Passes the complete pre-commit run and updates the rendered tool-calling documentation.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes the trigger, implementation, reproduction, validation, and duplicate-work checks.
</details>

files.patch:
@@ -109,6 +109,39 @@ vLLM supports the `tool_choice='none'` option in the chat completion API. When t
 !!! note
     When tools are specified in the request, vLLM includes tool definitions in the prompt by default, regardless of the `tool_choice` setting. To exclude tool definitions when `tool_choice='none'`, use the `--exclude-tools-when-tool-choice-none` option.
 
+## Allowed Tools in the Rust Frontend
+
+The Rust frontend accepts `tool_choice.allowed_tools` on `/v1/chat/completions`
+to restrict a request to a subset of its declared function tools. Without this
+option, the normal `tool_choice` behavior applies.
+
+For example, when `tools` declares both `get_weather` and `get_time`, this choice
+exposes only `get_time` to the chat renderer:
+
+```json
+{
+  "type": "allowed_tools",
+  "allowed_tools": {
+    "mode": "auto",
+    "tools": [
+      {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_time"}}
+    ]
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Pass this object as `tool_choice` alongside the request's `messages` and `tools`.
+Use `mode: "auto"` to allow a text response or tool calls, or `mode: "required"`
+to require tool calling from the allowed subset. Every allowed name must appear
+in the top-level `tools` list; a tool declared only in a developer message does
+not authorize an allowed name. Filtering also applies to developer-message tool
+declarations and preserves declaration order.
+
+An empty list in `auto` mode disables tool calling. An empty list in `required`
+mode, an undeclared function name, or an unsupported reference type returns an
+HTTP 400 error. This option does not change the tool parser and model setup
+needed for tool calling.
+
 ## Constrained Decoding Behavior
 
 Structural-tag parsers resolve call obligation, grammar activation, and argument-schema enforcement separately. With structural-tag enforcement enabled:
